title: Simon Boccanegra
subtitle: Bruson, Ricciarelli, Raimondi · Abbado
summary: Verdi's Simon Boccanegra (1881 version) at the Wiener Staatsoper on 22 March 1984. This was the Vienna premiere of the Strehler/Frigerio production, conducted by Claudio Abbado with Bruson, Ricciarelli, Raimondi and Luchetti. The 28 files are a track-for-track rip of the RCA Red Seal/BMG 'Wiener Staatsoper Live' 2-CD release 74321 57733-2 (1998) of Austrian Radio's (ORF) live recording of that night. They are not an off-air copy.
date_evidence: The folder '840322' means 1984-03-22. The Staatsoper's own per-performance record (s1, re-read by the reconciler) lists 22.03.1984, Thursday 19:00, as the PREMIERE of the new Simon Boccanegra production. The release notes say 'Live recording by Austrian Radio (ORF) on March 22 1984' (s3), and Operadis, Busse and the Wiener Philharmoniker discography all give 22 March 1984 (s6, s5, s14). The 28 file durations match the RCA 2-CD track list (s4), within about 1 s on 27 tracks and 3 s on one. The release has Luchetti as Adorno, who sang only on 22.03; Carreras sang Adorno from 25.03 on (s2, s12). That independently fits the stated date.
broadcaster: ORF (Austrian Radio) made the original live recording, per the release data (s3). No broadcast-day listing was found, so the air date is unknown.
event_name: Wiener Staatsoper: premiere of the new production (Giorgio Strehler staging, originally La Scala 1971)

program.title: Simon Boccanegra
program.notes: 1881 revised version (libretto by Piave, revised by Boito). Complete: prologue and three acts, about 134.7 min, sung in Italian.

credits.notes: Sang the premiere on 22.03.1984 only. José Carreras sang Adorno on 25, 28 and 31 March and 3 April 1984 (s2, s12). Busse spells the name 'Lucchetti'.

s1 has no orchestra row. The release credits (s3) and s12 name the house orchestra. s14 files it under 'Wiener Philharmoniker', whose players form the Staatsoper orchestra. No Wikidata QID was found.
The production originated at La Scala (1971) and was brought to Vienna (s7, s16).

open_questions: Play order: the folders are out of opera order. Folder B holds CD1 tracks 1-15 (Prologue and Act I up to 'Messeri, il re di Tartaria'). Folder A Track 01 is CD1 track 16 ('Plebe! Patrizi!', the end of Act I), and A Tracks 02-13 are CD2 (Acts II-III). Play B first, then A.
These files match the commercial CD, so this is not an off-air copy. Does the collector also hold an off-air ORF broadcast of this performance? No broadcast-day listing or ORF air date was found.

The release is said to be edited from the premiere alone (Discogs: 'Live recording by Austrian Radio (ORF) on March 22 1984'), but its 40-page booklet was not read. Patching from later performances cannot be fully ruled out. Luchetti, who sang only the premiere, is on the release, which argues against patching in any scene with Adorno.

No cast-change evidence was found for 22.03.1984. The official archive record shows no Umbesetzung. The contemporary OPERA review (June 1984 pp.631-632) and the Gramophone CD review (Feb 1999 p.96; site returned 403) were not read. The search budget ran out before Austrian press of March 1984 could be checked.

Release year: Discogs, MusicBrainz and the US copyright registration (publication 24 Nov 1998) give 1998. Operadis gives 1999, probably because its cited reviews appeared in early 1999. Recorded as 1998.
Disc 1 track 6 ('O de' Fieschi implacata') is 257 s on MusicBrainz but 253.9 s in the file (B/Track 06). Is the rip missing about 3 s of applause or lead-out, or is the MusicBrainz figure off?
The reconciler could not re-fetch s13 (cede.com, 403), s15 (Radio France, connection refused) or s16 (Die Presse, blocked). Their excerpts rest on Codex's reading. None is needed for any credit.
No Wikidata QIDs were found for the Staatsoper orchestra and chorus, or for Marise Flach. The QIDs for Sfiris and Aichberger point to sparse items matched by name only.
